The AP Chinese Language and Culture Exam has 2 sections and lasts approximately 1 hour and 50 minutes.

Section I: Free Response

The free-response section of the AP Chinese Language and Culture Exam includes 4 free-response questions and lasts approximately 45 minutes. 

Section I, Part A: Speaking

This part of the exam includes 2 free-response questions about your project. The part lasts approximately 15 minutes.

Section I, Part B: Writing

This part of the exam includes 2 free-response questions and lasts approximately 30 minutes. Both questions require written responses in Chinese.

Section II: Multiple Choice

The multiple-choice section of the exam includes 2 parts and lasts approximately 1 hour and 5 minutes.

Section II, Part A: Listening

This part of the exam includes 5 question sets, each containing 5 multiple-choice questions, and lasts approximately 25 minutes. Each set includes an audio source that you will use to answer the questions. Once timing for each set expires, you will automatically move on to the next set, and you will be unable to return to the prior set.

Section II, Part B: Reading

This part of the exam includes 6 question sets, each containing 5 multiple-choice questions, and lasts approximately 40 minutes. Each set includes reading material that you will use to answer the questions. Once time expires in this part, all the answers you have already selected will be automatically submitted, and you will be unable to return to the questions.

Day 2 of the AP Networking Exam consists of a multiple-choice section.

Multiple Choice

This section has 36 questions and lasts 1 hour. This section represents 50% of your total score. Your score on this section is based on the number of questions answered correctly. Points are not deducted for incorrect answers or unanswered questions.

Taking the Exam

You can go back and forth between questions in the section until time expires. The clock will turn red when 5 minutes remain—the proctor will not give you any time updates or warnings. Once time expires in the section, you cannot return to it.

A calculator is available in this application and can be accessed throughout the exam. 

You may use scratch paper for notes and planning, but credit will only be given for responses entered in this application. Any text you enter as an annotation will not be included in your answer submissions. When time expires in the section, all answers you have already entered will be submitted.

Begin audio description of Bluebook Testing Tools 

Section Directions: Directions are on the top left of each test screen. Find the show directions button in the exam player controls section. 

Testing Timer: Use the timer to pace yourself. You can hide it until 5 minutes remain. The hide/show buttons are in the timer section. 

Highlights & Notes: Click Highlights & Notes then select some text to get started. The Highlights & Notes button is in the test tools section. When activated, you can highlight text within the exam and create notes from the Highlight Options group of controls. 

Line Reader: Use the line reader to help you focus as you’re reading test content. Access the line reader from the More options region within the test tools section. 

Calculator: On the SAT Suite of Assessments and certain AP Exams, you’ll have access to a calculator. Some exams have more than one kind. The calculator and reference buttons are located in the test tools section. When activated, a region for the calculator or reference sheets is opened. 

Reference Sheet: Many exams have a reference sheet where you can find common formulas. 

Help: Click on More to access Help content. Access the More button and expanded options from the test tools section. 

Expand Left/Right: Grab the center line to expand either side of the screen. The separator control to expand the left and right panels is named "resize page content" and located between the passage and question regions of the page. 

Zoom: Zoom with keyboard shortcuts on laptops or by pinching on tablets. Quick Tip: Zoom using Control +/- (PC) or Command +/- (Mac). 

Mark for Review: Use the bookmark icon to flag any question you want to come back to. The mark for review button is located in the Question and Answer section. 

Option Eliminator: On multiple-choice questions, if you think an answer option is wrong, you can cross it out. The option eliminator push button is located in the Question and Answer section. When pressed, buttons to cross out or undo crossed-out options appear adjacent to each answer option. 

Question Menu: Navigate to any question in the section. The question navigator button is in the Question navigation section. When expanded, the book mark icon will appear in the question navigator to indicate questions that have been marked for review.

title: Reminder: Biometric Data for Test Security

content.content:
When registering for the SAT and selecting this test center outside of the United States, you provided your explicit consent to the collection and processing of your biometric data, including your facial image for facial recognition and keystroke data.

College Board may collect this biometric data to:

  • confirm the test taker is and remains the registered test taker
  • detect and prevent fraud and misrepresentation
  • maintain the integrity of the testing process
  • improve test security
  • detect and prevent misconduct and violations of SAT Testing Rules
  • process as permitted by law


College Board takes the privacy of our test takers seriously and protects your personal data with operational, administrative, technical, and physical security safeguards. You can review our full Privacy Statement and the Testing Rules at: privacy.collegeboard.org. 

If you wish to withdraw your consent to the collection and processing of your biometric data, please do not continue with the test and notify the test administrator now. You will not be able to take the SAT today, and the test administrator will provide you with College Board’s Customer Service contact information.

title: Get Ready for the Digital SAT

content.content:
If you’re taking the test on a weekend, here’s how it’ll work. 

Before test day, head to the Practice and Prepare section of the Bluebook homepage and start practicing. 

You can explore the tools and features of the app and try a few sample questions in the test preview or take a full-length practice test.  

The week of the test, you'll complete a quick exam setup to check your device and get your admission ticket.  

You’ll need this admission ticket on test day. You can take a picture of it, print it, or email it to yourself.   

Arrive on time on test day. Check your admission ticket for your arrival time and the address of your test center.  

Be sure to bring your fully charged device. It’ll need to stay on for roughly three hours, so we recommend you bring a power cord or portable charger. You’ll also need your admission ticket, a valid photo ID, and a pencil or pen. Scratch paper will be provided. 

The digital SAT has two sections—Reading and Writing, and Math. It should take you just over 2 hours to complete, not including breaks.   

Each section of the test has two parts called modules, and each module is timed separately. You can move back and forth between questions in a module and review your answers until time expires. There will be a break between sections. 

During the test, you’ll have access to a set of tools.   

On all math questions, you’ll find a reference sheet and a calculator. You can also bring an approved calculator.   

Click Highlights & Notes, then select some text to highlight, underline, or leave yourself a note. 

On multiple-choice questions, if you think an answer option is wrong, you can cross it out.  

You can use the line reader to help you focus as you’re reading test content.  

And you can mark for review any questions you want to come back to later. 

Zoom in and out using keyboard shortcuts on laptops or by pinching on tablets.  

If you have a problem during the test, click the Help icon for troubleshooting tips. And you can always raise your hand to ask the proctor for help, too.   

When the test is over, your answers will be submitted automatically. Wait until you see the “Congratulations” screen to close your device.  

We’re excited for you to take the digital SAT. Good luck on test day!

title: Keyboard Tips
body:
Special characters: Hold down keys for special characters, such as: é, ñ, ¿

Installing keyboards: If you don’t have your foreign language keyboard installed on your device, follow these steps.

   Windows

  • Open Settings then go to Time & Language > Language & region.

  • Click Add a language and select the desired language.

  • Click Next > Install.

    
    Mac

  • Open the Apple menu then click System Settings > Keyboard.

  • Click Input Sources > Add (+).

  • Select the desired language and click Add.
     

  iPad

  • Open Settings then go to General > Keyboard > Keyboards.

  • Click Add New Keyboard and select the desired language.

    
   Chromebook: If you don't have a foreign language keyboard installed on your device, please ask someone at your school for help.

Switching Keyboards: Use shortcuts to switch between English and foreign language keyboards.
 

  • Chromebook: Ctrl + Shift + Space
  • Windows: Alt + Shift
  • Mac: Ctrl + Space
  • iPad: Ctrl + Space or Globe icon

title: Microphone Tips
body:
If your microphone isn’t working and there’s another one you can use, please switch and see if that solves the problem. 

Otherwise, try these steps: 

  • Always allow microphone access when using Bluebook.
  • Make sure your microphone is fully plugged in and has no frayed or damaged wires.
  • Confirm you’ve selected the correct microphone under Keyboards & Audio.
  • Check that your volume isn’t muted/turned down. 

 

To allow microphone access, you may need to adjust your settings.

On a Windows device: 
Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone > Enable Let desktop apps access your microphone

On a Mac device:
Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone > Enable Bluebook

On an iPad:
Go to Settings > Apps > Bluebook > Allow Microphone

On a Chromebook:
Contact someone at your school for help.

Section Directions: Directions are on the top left of each test screen. Find the show directions button in the exam player controls section. 

Testing Timer: Use the timer to pace yourself. You can hide it until 5 minutes remain. The hide/show buttons are in the timer section. 

Highlights & Notes: Click Highlights & Notes then select some text to get started. The Highlights & Notes button is in the test tools section. When activated, you can highlight text within the exam and create notes from the Highlight Options group of controls. 

Line Reader: Use the line reader to help you focus as you're reading test content. Access the line reader from the More options region within the test tools section. 

Calculator: On the SAT Suite of Assessments and certain AP Exams, you'll have access to a calculator. Some exams have more than one kind.The calculator and reference buttons are located in the test tools section. When activated, a region for the calculator or reference sheets is opened. 

Reference Sheet: Many exams have a reference sheet where you can find common formulas. 

Help: Click on More to access help content. Access the More button and expanded options from the test tools section. 

Expand Left/Right: Grab the center line to expand either side of the screen. The separator control to expand the left and right panels is named "resize page content" and located between the passage and question regions of the page. 

Zoom: Zoom with keyboard shortcuts on laptops or by pinching on tablets. 

Mark for Review: Use the bookmark icon to flag any question you want to come back to. The mark for review button is located in the Question and Answer section. 

Option Eliminator: On multiple-choice questions, if you think an answer option is wrong, you can cross it out. The option eliminator push button is located in the Question and Answer section. When pressed, buttons to cross out or undo crossed-out options appear adjacent to each answer option. 

Question Menu: Navigate to any question in the module or part. The question navigator button is in the Question navigation section. When expanded, the bookmark icon will appear in the question navigator to indicate questions that have been marked for review.

The SAT with Essay has three sections: Reading and Writing, Math, and the Essay.

Section 1: Reading and Writing (66 Questions)

There are two modules in the Reading and Writing section. Each module has 33 questions.

Section 2: Math (54 Questions)

There are two modules in the Math section. Each module has 27 questions.

Section 3: Essay 

There is one module in the Essay section.

Modules

Within each section, the modules are timed separately. If time permits, you can review your answers in a given module. When the timer reaches zero, you will automatically move on. Once you move on from any module, you cannot return to it.

Directions

Directions for answering the questions appear at the start of each section. You can find these directions at the top-left corner of every question screen.
If you’re approved for text-to-speech, use this tool on test day to hear entire passages or specific sentences.
You can resume this practice test as soon as you’re ready to move on. On test day, you’ll wait until the clock counts down. Read below to see how breaks work on test day.
content.title: Test Preview Break

content.content:
Place your exam booklet on your desk now.

Follow these rules during the break:

  1. Do not disturb students who are still testing.
  2. Do not exit the app or close your laptop.
  3. Do not access phones, smartwatches, textbooks, notes, or the internet.
  4. Do not eat or drink in the test room.
  5. Do not speak in the test room; outside the test room, do not discuss the exam with anyone.

title: Verbal Instructions: Hybrid
body:
[Note: These instructions may vary slightly from what the proctor reads.] 

Your proctor will read this aloud:  

Welcome. If you haven’t completed check-in yet, pause while I read. You can finish checking in later. 

Today you’re taking a digital AP Exam. The exam has two sections with a break in between. This is a hybrid digital exam, so each section works differently, so listen carefully. 

Section I is multiple choice, and you’ll use Bluebook on your device to read the exam questions and enter your answers. Section II is free response; you’ll still read the questions in Bluebook but write your answers in the free-response booklet. 

Remember, you agreed to follow rules preventing students from having an unfair advantage. I will dismiss anyone who tries to break those rules, and their scores will be canceled. They may also be prevented from taking College Board exams in the future. 

Bluebook should be the only application open on your device unless you’re using approved assistive technology. Close all other applications now. You might need to quit Bluebook first and reopen it when you finish. 

You should have the following items on your desk: 

  • Your testing device 
  • 2 black or dark blue pens or No. 2 pencils 
  • A free-response booklet  
  • Your AP ID label sheet 
  • 2 sheets of scratch paper 
  • An exam-specific reference information booklet [not applicable for Calculus, Macroeconomics, or Microeconomics] 


Make sure your free-response booklet has the name of this exam and today’s date on the front cover. 

When using your printed reference information booklet, you may use the margins or any blank space for scratch work as well.  

You’re allowed 2 handheld calculators. Store your backup calculator under your desk. You may also use the built-in Desmos calculator available in Bluebook. In Section II, you’ll need a pen or pencil to write your responses. If you use a pencil, be sure that your writing is dark enough to read easily. To avoid scoring problems, don’t write in multiple colors. 

Now, check that your AP ID label sheet has your name printed at the top. 

Raise your hand if you need a pen or pencil or if there are any issues with your materials. 

In Section II, you’ll need a pen or pencil to write your responses. If you use a pencil, be sure that your writing is dark enough to read easily. To avoid scoring problems, don’t write in multiple colors. 

Now, check that your AP ID label sheet has your name printed at the top. 

Raise your hand if you need a pen or pencil or if there are any issues with your materials. 

You should also have 2 sheets of scratch paper, which I’ll collect after the exam, so don’t tear them. Now, write your full name, today’s date, and the exam name in the top right corner of both sheets.  

You can use the scratch paper for notes and planning your responses, but no credit will be given for anything written on scratch paper.   

In Section II, your answers and any work you’re asked to show must be written in the free-response booklet, as specified in the directions in Bluebook.   

Now it’s time to label your free-response booklet. Listen carefully to my instructions. 

First, complete the information on the front cover. For step 3, you’ll need your school code; it’s printed in the top right corner of your AP ID label sheet.  

Next, place an AP ID label in the space provided and read the information on the right. Look up when you finish. 

Make sure the subject listed on your reference information booklets matches the exam you’re taking. Write your name in the space provided on the cover of the booklet, and write the date next to it. 

Are there any questions? 

Then your proctor will read this: 

[For Physics and Chemistry only: In Section II, the free-response section, the questions in Bluebook include instructions telling you which page in your booklet to write your answers on. Make sure you write your answers on the correct page in the booklet.] 

[For Macroeconomics or Microeconomics only: In Section II, the free-response section, start your response to each question on a new page. At the top of each page, fill in the circle for the question number you’re answering on that page. If you fill in the wrong circle, cross it out neatly with an X, and fill in the correct circle.] 

When you use the free-response booklet during Section II, make sure you write your answers in the correct place. If you start to answer on the wrong page, you may cross it out and write it on the correct page. 

Make sure to keep an eye on the timer in Bluebook while writing and stop when time runs out. 

If you run out of space, raise your hand and I’ll give you extra paper. 

[For Calculus only: Now listen carefully to these calculator rules: 

  • Sections I and II both have a part A and a part B. 
  • There’s a 1-minute pause between parts. 
  • In each section, graphing calculators are needed in one part and prohibited in the other. 
  • You’ll see reminders in Bluebook and your free-response booklet whenever calculators are prohibited.  
  • You can use your own calculator or the one available in Bluebook.] 

 
Are there any questions? 

Then your proctor will read this: 

Place your free-response booklet under your chair and leave it there until your break. Leave your AP ID label sheet on your desk so I can collect it.  

I’ll come around now to make sure you cleared your desk as instructed in Bluebook. And if you brought a calculator, I’ll make sure it’s acceptable. 

If you still have prohibited items, turn them off and put them on your desk so I can collect them. 

After your proctor checks student desks, they’ll read this:  

Please give me your attention again. 

Bluebook will end Section I and start your break automatically. You might start your break at slightly different times than your neighbor, so please be quiet at all times. 

When your break starts, leave your calculator on your desk and place your free-response booklet on your desk. Don’t take your booklet, calculator, or scratch paper out of the room. 

When your break ends, click Resume Testing and take a few minutes to read the Section II directions before you click Resume Testing again and start your timer. I’m going to repeat that important tip: to save testing time, read the free-response directions before your countdown clock starts. 

To take a break at any other time, go to the More menu and click Unscheduled Break. Raise your hand and wait for me to dismiss you if you want to leave the room. You’ll lose testing time if you take an unscheduled break. 

If you have an approved accommodation for breaks as needed, select Pause under the timer so you don’t lose testing time. 

I’ll give you the start code after I read these final instructions. 

If you see the low-battery warning on your screen, raise your hand so I can help you. Keep your laptop open or your tablet uncovered until I dismiss you. I’ve written a reminder here. 

When your exam ends, sit quietly until I make sure your answers were submitted and collect your materials. Remember that others may still be testing.  

Raise your hand at any time if you need help or more scratch paper. In Section II, raise your hand if you need extra paper to finish writing your response.  

[For Calculus only: Now, place your calculators under your desk and leave them there until Section I Part B.] 

Are there any questions? 

After your proctor pauses to answer questions, they’ll read this:   

When you enter the code and click Start Test, your timer will start and you can begin testing. 

If you don’t see the start code screen yet, finish checking in.  

I’ll read the start code now and write it on the board. Good luck!

title: Ending the Test Early
body: If you're approved for extra time, you can move on from a section or end the test before your full time expires, though we encourage you to use extra time to check your work. You must use the standard time for a section before you can move on. When the standard time has elapsed, the Next button on the Check Your Work page will become active. Once you move on from any section of the test, you cannot go back.

title: Take a Break: Do Not Close Your Device

content.content:
Place your exam booklet on your desk now.

Follow these rules during the break:

  1. Do not disturb students who are still testing.
  2. Do not exit the app or close your laptop.
  3. Do not access phones, smartwatches, textbooks, notes, or the internet.
  4. Do not eat or drink in the test room.
  5. Do not speak in the test room; outside the test room, do not discuss the exam with anyone.

help_items.title: Zoom and Magnification
help_items.body:
Chromebook Zoom and Magnification

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use the magnification feature, select the options from the floating accessibility menu:

  • Full-screen magnifier (Search + Ctrl + M) — whole-screen magnification
    • Adjust the full-screen magnifier from the floating Accessibility menu > Settings > Display and magnification > Full screen magnifier > select any of these options:
      • Move screen continuously as mouse moves
      • Move screen keeping mouse at center of screen
      • Move screen when mouse touches edge of screen (default)
  • Docked magnifier (Search + Ctrl + D) — split-screen magnification
    • To adjust zoom level, select the down arrow in the Docked zoom level.
    • To change what’s magnified, move your pointer or press Tab.

 

Windows Zoom and Magnifier

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use Windows Magnifier:  

  • Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Vision: Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Or press the Windows logo key + plus sign (+). To turn off the Magnifier, press the Windows logo key + Esc.

Adjust the Magnifier view per your preference:  

  • Lens (Ctrl + Alt + L)
  • Full screen (Ctrl + Alt + F)
  • Docked (Ctrl + Alt + D)

 

MacOS Zoom

To zoom in/out, press Command +/-. To reset zoom, press Command + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To customize how the zoom area appears, go to Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility and click Zoom on the right (keyboard shortcut: Option + Command + 8).

In the Advanced Options, select the checkboxes for your zoom preference:  

  • Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom
  • Use trackpad gesture to zoom
  • Use scroll gesture with modifier keys to zoom

Select Zoom style options per student preference:  

  • Full screen
  • Split screen
  • Picture-in-picture

 

iPad Zoom

Pinch to zoom in or zoom out.

For additional zoom options in the iPad, tap Settings > Accessibility > Zoom.

Adjust any of the following:

  • Keyboard shortcuts: Control zoom using shortcuts on an external keyboard.
  • Zoom controller: Turn the controller on, set controller actions, and adjust the color and opacity.
  • Zoom region: Choose Pinned Zoom, Full Screen Zoom, or Window Zoom.
  • Zoom filters: Choose None, Inverted, Grayscale, Grayscale Inverted, or Low Light.
  • Maximum zoom level: Drag the slider to adjust the level.

help_items.body:
During testing, a timer will let you know how much time remains for each module or part of the test.

title: Section Directions: Reading and Writing
body:
Each question includes one or more passages, which may include a table or graph. Read each passage and question carefully, and then choose the best answer to the question based on the passage(s).  

All questions in this section are multiple-choice with four answer choices. Each question has a single best answer.

title: Section Directions: Math
body:
The questions in this section address a number of important math skills. 

Use of a calculator is permitted for all questions. A reference sheet, calculator, and these directions can be accessed throughout the test. 

Unless otherwise indicated: 

  • All variables and expressions represent real numbers. 

  • Figures provided are drawn to scale. 

  • All figures lie in a plane. 

  • The domain of a given function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.  

For multiple-choice questions, solve each problem and choose the correct answer from the choices provided. Each multiple-choice question has a single correct answer. 

For student-produced response questions, solve each problem and enter your answer as described below. 

  • If you find more than one correct answer, enter only one answer. 

  • You can enter up to 5 characters for a positive answer and up to 6 characters (including the negative sign) for a negative answer. 

  • If your answer is a fraction that doesn’t fit in the provided space, enter the decimal equivalent. 

  • If your answer is a decimal that doesn’t fit in the provided space, enter it by truncating or rounding at the fourth digit. 

  • If your answer is a mixed number (such as 3 ½), enter it as an improper fraction (7/2) or its decimal equivalent (3.5). 

  • Don’t enter symbols such as a percent sign, comma, or dollar sign.

help_items.title: Approved Calculators
help_items.body:
Acceptable Calculators

Calculators permitted during testing include:

  • The Desmos calculator embedded in the Bluebook testing app: This is a powerful calculator that includes features similar to a handheld graphing calculator. If you are familiar with how to use this calculator, the embedded version is a good choice.
  • Graphing calculators that do not include CAS features: This type of calculator includes plotting and graphing windows, data entry and storage windows, data analysis functions, trig functions, and programming options.
  • Scientific calculators: This type of calculator includes many functions helpful for solving problems in science, statistics, and math. Common features include built-in memory to store interim calculations, statistical functions, pi, trig functions, and scientific notation.
  • Four-function basic calculators (not recommended): This type of calculator includes four functions: add, subtract, multiply, and divide; some also include percentages and square roots. This type of calculator is not recommended as they typically do not follow order of operations.
     

Prohibited Calculators

Calculators with the following features are prohibited:

  • Calculators with built-in CAS functionality. Examples of such devices include:
    • Casio: ClassPad 300, 330, or 400; ClassPad II (fx-CP400); ClassPad fx-CG 500 or fx-CG500; Algebra fx 2.0; all model numbers that begin with CFX-9970G.
    • Hewlett Packard: HP Prime; HP 48GII; all model numbers that begin with 40G, 49G, or 50G.
    • Texas Instruments: TI-Nspire CAS, TI-Nspire CX II CAS; All model numbers that begin with TI-89 or TI-92 or have "CAS" in the model name. Note that TI-Nspire models that do not include "CAS" in the name are acceptable.
  • Calculators with apps, menus, or programs that perform symbolic algebra manipulation (e.g., solving algebra equations symbolically).
  • Calculators with QWERTY keyboards.
  • Devices with wireless internet capability, Bluetooth, or cellular connectivity.
  • Devices with built-in cameras or audio/video recording.
  • Tablets and laptop computers.
  • Electronic writing pads or pen-input devices.
  • Cell phone calculator apps.
  • Calculators that use paper tape.

help_items.title: Verbal Instructions: PSAT/NMSQT
help_items.body:
Your proctor will read this aloud: 
 
Welcome. Today you’re taking the Preliminary SAT/National Merit Scholarship Qualifying Test, also known as the PSAT/NMSQT, which focuses on what you’re learning in high school. It’s also a chance to practice for the SAT and qualify for scholarship programs. 

Please listen carefully to these instructions. When I finish, I’ll give you the start code. If you haven’t completed check-in yet, pause while I read. You can finish later. 

If you’d like to follow along as I read these instructions, click Review the Instructions. If you’re not on the start code screen yet, click Help and then Verbal Instructions. 

You agreed to follow the rules and keep test content confidential. I will dismiss anyone who tries to break the rules, and their scores will be canceled. They may also be prevented from taking College Board tests in the future. 

Bluebook should be the only application open on your device unless you’re using approved assistive technology. Other open applications will be detected and could result in score cancellation. 

Close all other applications now. You might need to quit Bluebook first and reopen it when you finish. Does anyone need to close other applications? 

Your proctor will pause so you can close any other applications, then they’ll read this: 
 
The test has 2 sections, with a break in between. Bluebook times everyone individually, and it will tell you when it’s time to take a break. To take a break at any other time, go to the More menu and click Unscheduled Break. You will lose testing time if you take an unscheduled break. 

If you have an approved accommodation for breaks as needed, select Pause under the timer instead so you don’t lose testing time. 

It’s important to leave your device open during the whole test, including breaks. 

I’ll come around now to collect prohibited devices and make sure you followed the Bluebook instructions for clearing your desk. I’ll also give you any materials related to your accommodations. 

If you have phones, smartwatches, or other prohibited devices, turn them off now. 

And if you brought a calculator, I’ll make sure it’s acceptable. 

You should have 3 sheets of scratch paper. Write your full name in the top right corner of each sheet. After the test you’ll need to return all 3 sheets of paper, and they can’t be torn.  

If students in your room are approved for certain accommodations, you'll hear additional instructions: 

For students testing with a screen reader: If you’re using a screen reader or other approved assistive technology, now is the time to make sure it’s working. Remember, you can use the built-in features on your device. More information is available on the Bluebook Help page. 

For students testing with a human reader: Readers must read questions aloud as often as requested. It’s important that they read only exactly what is in the script. They must not elaborate, even if the student asks. 

For students testing with a scribe: Scribes must write only the answers and corrections that students dictate. They can’t prompt the student in a way that would result in a different response. Scribes will read student answers back to them if students want to review their work. 

For students testing with raised line drawings: The raised line drawings have the same labels and numbers as the detailed descriptions you’ll hear. 

Your proctor will collect any prohibited items, then they’ll read this: 
Please pay attention to these important reminders. 

To avoid scoring problems, don’t close Bluebook or your device until you see the Congratulations screen. If your time runs out and you don’t see that screen, raise your hand so I can help you finish. Otherwise, sit quietly with your device open until I dismiss you. 

Also, be quiet at all times because you might start your break and finish your test at slightly different times than your neighbor.  

If you need help at any time, raise your hand and I’ll come over. Does anyone have any questions?  

Your proctor will answer any final questions, then they’ll read this: 
 
I’ll give you the start code in a moment. When you enter the code and click Start Test, your timer will start and you can begin testing. 

If you don’t see the start code screen yet, finish checking in to Bluebook.  

I’ll read the start code now and write it on the board. Good luck!

help_items.title: Digital Testing Accommodations: SAT Suite
help_items.body:
Some testing accommodations work differently on the digital SAT than on the paper version of the test. Other accommodations may not be needed for a digital SAT. On your personal info page, Bluebook will list only the accommodations that apply to your digital SAT. 

If you’re approved for one of these accommodations, here’s how it’ll work in Bluebook.

AccommodationHow it Works in Bluebook
Extended Time

You’ll receive your approved amount of extended time and extra breaks. Once the standard time has elapsed on a module, section or part, you can move on when you are ready. 

Extended time for reading will be applied to the entire test. Extended time for math will only be applied to the Math section. Note: For SAT Weekend, if you’re approved for up to time and one-half and double time, you’ll test in a test center on a Saturday or Sunday.

Breaks as NeededYou’ll be able to pause the test time to take breaks as needed. The pause button appears below the timer. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra BreaksYou’ll get an extra 5-minute break between modules 1 and 2 in each section. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra and Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’, and you’ll have extra breaks. There is no pause button; you simply take the extra breaks for the length of time applied in Bluebook.
Braille (Refreshable Braille for Digital)You can use a screen reader, text-to-speech or refreshable braille. If you use a screen reader or text-to-speech, you’ll need to use headphones, too.  
Raised Line DrawingsYou’ll take the test in Bluebook, and you’ll receive a raised line supplement.
Braille WriterYou’ll use braille writing software to take the test.
Large-Print Exam, Large Print Answer Sheet, Magnification Device (Electronic/Non-Electronic)You can zoom using your device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).
Color Overlay/Color ContrastYou can use the color settings available through your operating system and/or device screen, or you can use a plastic overlay attached to your device's screen.
Human Reader for Digital Tests

Most students who use a human reader for paper exams are approved for Text-to-Speech (Embedded) and/or Screen Reader (Non-Embedded) for digital tests and will test digitally. You will use the built-in text-to-speech tool in Bluebook or the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board–approved screen reader software. In rare conditions, a student who is unable to test with text-to-speech or a screen reader may be approved in SSD Online for the accommodation of human reader for digital tests. 

Screen Reader (Non-Embedded)You can use the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board approved screen reader software (JAWS, NVDA, etc.). In addition to reading all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers), your screen reader will also read all properties of the page (headers, footers, punctuation) and provide detailed descriptions of graphs and figures. And you’ll get time and one-half (+50%) on your test.  
Text-to-Speech (Embedded) You can use the text-to-speech tool in Bluebook to read all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers) and short descriptions of graphics. 
Human Scribe for Digital Assessments You can use a human scribe to record the responses in Bluebook. You will test in a one-to-one setting. 
Dictation for Digital ExamsYou can use speech-to-text functionality on your test. Note: This is not a tool within the Bluebook application; it is the same functionality that you use with other applications.
Assistive Technology (AT)You can use your approved assistive technology software.
4-Function CalculatorYou can use a calculator on all math questions on the test. Use the Desmos calculator that’s built into the app, or bring your own approved calculator.
Limited TimeIf the test time exceeds your approved time, you will test over multiple days.
Auditory Amplification/FM SystemYou can test with your FM system, and you can use headphones. The proctor should use a handheld mic to give you the instructions.

help_items.title: Assistive Technology
help_items.body:
Any approved assistive technology that you use when you’re online should still work during your exam. If you use assistive technologies (AT), such as screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, ChromeVox, ZoomText Fusion, etc.) to interact with a standard web browser, the same commands can be used to navigate through content in the digital exam. The exception to this would be if you use a web-based assistive technology or a browser extension.

If you use assistive technology, open/start the AT device or software before you open Bluebook for practice and on exam day. On exam day, adjust any necessary settings before you start to check in for the digital exam. Exceptions are noted when configuration is not required ahead of the exam.

help_items.title: MathJax
help_items.body:
Bluebook implements MathJax technology to: 

  • Display mathematical content, such as expressions, equations, and inequalities elegantly in browsers. 
  • Provide students who use screen readers with MathCAT access to off-screen accessible MathML for both UEB and Nemeth braille support with refreshable braille displays. 
  • Access a variety of accessibility features via menus attached to the MathJax content to assist students with low vision and students that need highlighted rendering. 
     

MathJax objects within Bluebook exams are custom-configured to function with all mainstream text-to-speech and screen-reading assistive technologies across all supported operating systems. This custom configuration ensures that all mainstream assistive technologies will read the textual alternatives without additional configurations. 
 

Optional MathJax configurations (UEB Support)  
Some students may prefer to navigate complex math equations and math expressions with math viewers or plugins like MathCAT with personal screen readers like JAWS and NVDA.   
To explore MathML content, you can press Alt + M (Windows and Chromebook) or Option + M (Mac and iOS) to turn graphic mode on/off. When graphic mode is turned off, students can access the MathML and choose UEB or Nemeth from MathCAT. 

Alternatively, hidden MathML can be enabled via the MathJax context menu via Options > Include Hidden MathML
 
NOTE: This action can be set once at the start of an exam, and it will persist throughout the duration. The student may press Alt + M (or Option + M) again to revert to the default “graphic mode on” configuration or by activating Reset to defaults within the MathJax Settings (context menu).

help_items.title: Screen Readers
help_items.body:
Chromebook ChromeVox

To enable ChromeVox, press Ctrl + Alt + Z or select it from the floating accessibility menu.

Note: If you're approved to use a screen reader and you don't see the floating accessibility menu on your Chromebook, let someone at your school know right away.

If ChromeVox turns off when you launch the Bluebook app or at any time, you can turn it back on with Ctrl + Alt + Z.

Test content can be navigated with the keyboard. Depending on your keyboard, you can press the Search or Launcher key for some shortcuts. Both keys work the same way.

 

Basic keyboard navigation: Use the keyboard shortcuts if parts of the content are not initially reading.
ActionKeyboard Shortcut
Read items on a pageSearch or Launcher + right arrow (or left arrow to move back)
Go to the next/previous lineSearch or Launcher + up/down arrow
Start reading from the current locationSearch or Launcher + R
Stop/pause readingCtrl

 

Windows Narrator

To start or stop Narrator, press the Windows logo key + Ctrl + Enter together. 

Important: The Narrator key is a modifier key in the Narrator commands. Both the Caps Lock and Insert keys are the Narrator key by default. The Narrator key is referred to as “Narrator” in commands.

 

Basic keyboard navigation:
ActionKeyboard Shortcut
Start or stop NarratorWindows logo key + Ctrl + Enter
Exit NarratorNarrator + Esc
Move to the next itemNarrator + right arrow
Move to the previous itemNarrator + left arrow
Start reading continuouslyNarrator + down arrow or Narrator + R
Stop/pause readingCtrl

 

MacOS VoiceOver

To start using VoiceOver:

Choose Apple menu > System Settings, then click Accessibility in the sidebar. Click VoiceOver on.

Press Command + F5 with the keyboard to turn VoiceOver on/off.

 

Basic keyboard navigation: VO is an abbreviation for VoiceOver keys Control + Option.
ActionKeyboard Command
Turn the screen reader on/offCommand + F5
Stop/pause readingCtrl
Read next/previous itemVO + right arrow/left arrow
Read the next focusable item (e.g., link, button)Tab
Start reading continuously from this point onVO + A

 

iPad VoiceOver

To start using VoiceOver: Go to Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver, then on or off.

iPad Only: Navigating Multiple-Choice Answer Options

  • Keyboard-only users can navigate to a radio button option with the Tab key.
  • More radio button options can be accessed with the Tab key and the spacebar to make an explicit selection.
  • Alternatively, keyboard-only users can navigate through multiple-choice options with Option + arrow keys or Control + arrow keys.

help_items.title: Text-to-Speech
help_items.body:
If you’re approved for the accommodation “Text-to-Speech (Embedded),” then a built-in text-to-speech (TTS) tool will be available whenever you test with Bluebook. You don’t need to do anything to configure this tool.  

Use the Play/Pause button to hear entire passages or engage Click Mode to hear specific sentences. 

You can adjust voice selection, speed, or volume of the playback.

If you're testing on a Mac or iPad and you're approved for embedded text-to-speech, you can now choose from any voices previously downloaded to the device in addition to standard Bluebook options.

help_items.title: Speech-to-Text
help_items.body:
Chromebook Dictation

Chromebook provides two options for using the dictation feature for items requiring text entry:  

  • Dictation: From the floating accessibility menu, select Dictation.
  • Speak with the onscreen keyboard: From the floating accessibility menu select Onscreen keyboard. At the top of the onscreen keyboard, select Speak (microphone).
    • You can move, float, dock, and resize the onscreen keyboard. 


Tap or select where you want to type (input field, free-response questions, essays, etc.). Press Search + D or  Launcher + D.

 

Windows Speech

To use Windows Speech, follow the steps below for your operating system:

Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Speech > Turn on Speech Recognition.

Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Speech > Turn on Voice Access.

  • Keyboard shortcut: Press Windows logo key + Ctrl + S to turn on speech recognition.


Tip: For Windows 10 or 11, to help with navigation and selecting elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “19, OK”).

 

MacOS Voice Control

To use Voice Control on a Mac, go to System Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control.

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Voice Control Guide > Open Guide.

 

iPad Voice Control

To start using Voice Control on an iPad, go to Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control. 

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Open Voice Control Guide.

help_items.title: Refreshable Braille Displays
help_items.body:
RBDs are used to read text-only content on digital exams. Alternative text descriptions are embedded in the exams for all graphics. RBDs must be properly set up before they can be used by students. For information about installing and setting up RBDs, refer to the product’s provided instructions and manuals.

Refreshable braille is not recommended for students that require tactile graphics. Students can request a braille exam or raised line drawings.

help_items.title: Screen Magnification
help_items.body: Screen magnification technology enlarges the content displayed on the computer screen in order to assist students with visual impairments. Although the exam app supports some non-embedded screen magnifier tools from third parties, all users can zoom using their device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).

help_items.title: Open Source Libraries
help_items.body: To view a list of third-party software that may be contained in portions of the Bluebook application, go to collegeboard.org/opensource. We’re grateful to the open source community for making this work available.

title: Verbal Instructions
body:
If you're taking the PSAT/NMSQT, your proctor will read this introduction:
Welcome. Today you’re taking the Preliminary SAT/National Merit Scholarship Qualifying Test, also known as the PSAT/NMSQT, which focuses on what you’re learning in high school. It’s also a chance to practice for the SAT and qualify for scholarship programs.

If you're taking the PSAT 10, your proctor will read this introduction:
Welcome. Today you're taking the PSAT 10, which focuses on what you're learning in school. It’s also a chance to see where you might need to improve in high school.

If you’re taking the PSAT 8/9, your proctor will read this introduction:
Welcome. Today you’re taking the PSAT 8/9, which focuses on what you’re learning in school. It’s also a chance to see where you might need to improve in high school.

Then your proctor will read this: 
Please listen carefully to these instructions. When I finish, I’ll give you the start code. If you haven’t completed check-in yet, pause while I read. You can finish checking in later.

If you’d like to follow along as I read these instructions, click Review the Instructions. If you’re not on the start code screen yet, click Help and then Verbal Instructions.

You agreed to follow the rules and keep test content confidential. I will dismiss anyone who tries to break the rules, and their scores will be canceled. They may also be prevented from taking College Board tests in the future.

Bluebook should be the only application open on your device unless you’re using approved assistive technology. Other open applications will be detected and could result in your score being canceled. Close all other applications now. 

Your proctor will pause so you can close any other applications, then they’ll read this:
Does anyone need more time to close other applications?

Bluebook times everyone individually and will tell you when it’s time to take your break. You might start your break at slightly different times than your neighbor, so please be quiet at all times.

To take a break at any other time, go to the More menu and click Unscheduled Break. You’ll lose testing time if you take an unscheduled break.

If you have an approved accommodation for breaks as needed, select Pause under the timer instead so you don’t lose testing time.

I’ll come around soon to make sure you cleared your desk as instructed in Bluebook. I’ll also give you any materials related to your accommodations. And if you brought a calculator, I’ll make sure it’s acceptable.

If you have phones, smartwatches, or other prohibited devices, turn them off and put them away now.

You should have 1 sheet of scratch paper, which I'll collect after the test so don't tear it. Write your full name in the top right corner. If you don't have one, let me know when I come by your desk.

If students in your room are approved for certain accommodations, you'll hear additional instructions:

For students testing with a screen reader: If you’re using a screen reader or other approved assistive technology, now is the time to make sure it’s working. If you customized your settings during practice, you may need to repeat this step now. Remember, you can use the built-in features on your device. More information is available on the Bluebook Help page.

For students testing with a human reader: Readers must read questions aloud as often as requested. It’s important that they read only exactly what is in the script. They must not elaborate, even if the student asks.

For students testing with a scribe: Scribes must write only the answers and corrections that students dictate. They can’t prompt the student in a way that would result in a different response. Scribes will read student answers back to them if students want to review their work.

For students testing with raised line drawings: The raised line drawings have the same labels and numbers as the detailed descriptions you’ll hear.

Then your proctor will read this:
Please pay attention to these final instructions.

Don’t leave until I confirm your answers are submitted and dismiss you. Don’t close your laptop or cover your tablet before then. I’ve posted a reminder here.

If you're taking the PSAT/NMSQT, your proctor will read this:
If you want to cancel your scores, let me know in the next 10 days.

Then your proctor will read this:
If you need help or extra scratch paper at any time, raise your hand and I’ll come over. Remember to write your full name on extra scratch paper.

Does anyone have any questions? 

Your proctor will answer any final questions, then they’ll read this:
I’ll give you the start code in a moment. When you enter the code and click Start Test, your timer will start and you can begin testing.

If you don’t see the start code screen yet, finish checking in. 

I’ll read the start code now and write it on the board. Good luck!

Part A: Multiple Choice

The multiple-choice part has 60 questions and lasts 1 hour and 10 minutes. This part represents 60% of your total score. Your score on the multiple-choice part is based on the number of questions answered correctly. Points are not deducted for incorrect answers or unanswered questions.

Part B: Short Answer

The short-answer part includes 1 question about a source for your course project. This part lasts 10 minutes and represents 1.5% of your total score.

Taking the Exam

Each part is timed separately. You can go back and forth between questions in a part until time expires. The clock will turn red when 5 minutes remain in a part—the proctor will not give you any time updates or warnings. You cannot move ahead to a different part. Once time expires in a part, you cannot return to it.

You may use scratch paper for notes and planning, but credit will only be given for responses entered in this application. Any text you enter as an annotation will not be included in your answer submissions. When time expires in a part, all answers you have already entered will be submitted.

The inclusion of source material in this exam is not intended as an endorsement by College Board of the content, ideas, or values expressed in the material. AP students are not expected or asked to subscribe to any specific cultural or political values, but they are expected to analyze perspectives that may be different from their own and to analyze and interpret sources in their historical and disciplinary contexts.

content.content: The test is complete, and your answers have been submitted.

Your proctor will dismiss you when it’s time to go. 

Please be quiet; other students may still be testing.

We’re going to ask a few questions about you. All questions are optional. By providing your information, you consent to collection, use, and disclosure by College Board of your personally identifiable information as further described below. If any of your answers differ from answers you gave us on previous in-school tests, we'll use your latest information. 

How will we use this information? College Board may use the information you provide:  

  • To verify your identity  
  • To administer this test, including with any necessary third parties
  • To provide your score information  
  • To maintain the fairness and validity of our tests  
  • For test security purposes  
  • For test accommodations purposes   
  • On a de-identified basis, for psychometric and educational research purposes, to demonstrate the effectiveness of our programs and services, and to maintain, develop, support, improve, and diagnose our services and applications  
  • To disclose as required by law, when we believe in good faith that it’s necessary to protect our rights, protect an individual’s safety or the safety of others, investigate fraud, or respond to a government request  

Who else can see this information? Your high school, school district, and state may receive your responses. We also send your scores and information to certain scholarship programs, unless you choose to opt out by contacting College Board’s Customer Service. This includes your state scholarship organization, if any, and the U.S. Presidential Scholars Program if you took the SAT test in the U.S., U.S. territories, or Puerto Rico, or are a U.S. citizen taking the test abroad. If you request that we send your SAT score(s) to colleges or other organizations, we send your scores, the mailing address you may choose to provide as part of this test, along with other information about you as further described in the Testing Rules for this test. Institutions that receive your information are required to keep it confidential and to follow College Board guidelines for using this information.  

We’ll share college and career recommendations with you. If you choose to use BigFuture School, we may use your information to verify your identity to access BigFuture School and provide you with information and recommendations about college and career options. If you opt in to Connections, we’ll use your information to deliver content from nonprofit colleges and universities, nonprofit scholarship providers, and government agencies running educational programs, which may be a good fit for you. Note: your school, district, or state may choose to not provide access to Connections for its students or students who test at their schools. 

Your privacy matters to us. College Board recognizes the importance of protecting your privacy. title: AP Exam or practice
body:
If you’re taking an AP Exam, sign in to Bluebook with your College Board account.

If you don’t have a College Board account, or you’re having trouble signing in, go to collegeboard.org and sign in there first. 

Once you’re signed in to Bluebook, you can take an AP exam preview. You can find other practice resources in AP Classroom.

title: PSAT/NMSQT, PSAT 10, PSAT 8/9, or practice
body:
If you’re taking one of the PSAT-related assessments, someone at your school will give you a sign-in ticket. Use the info on that ticket to sign in to Bluebook.

If you don’t have a sign-in ticket yet, ask someone at your school for help.

If you take a full-length practice test in Bluebook, use the same info from your sign-in ticket to log in to My Practice to check your scores.

title: SAT School Day or SAT practice
body:
If you’re taking the SAT on a school day, someone at your school will give you a sign-in ticket. Use the info on that ticket to sign in to Bluebook.

If you don’t have a sign-in ticket yet, ask someone at your school for help.

If you take an SAT full-length practice test in Bluebook, use the same info from your sign-in ticket to log in to My Practice to check your scores.

title: SAT Weekend or SAT practice
body:
If you’re taking the SAT on the weekend or you want to take an SAT practice test, sign in to Bluebook with your College Board account.

If you don’t have a College Board account, or you’re having trouble signing in, go to collegeboard.org and sign in there first. 

If you take a full-length SAT practice test in Bluebook, use your College Board account to log in to My Practice to check your scores.

title: If You’re Taking a PSAT/NMSQT, PSAT 10, or PSAT 8/9
body:
If you're registered for any PSAT-related assessment, your school will give you a sign-in ticket that you’ll use to access Bluebook. Then you'll see your test listed on the homepage. 

If you signed in with a College Board account, you need to sign out and then sign back in using your sign-in ticket.

If your test is still not showing up, please contact your teacher or someone at your school.

title: Full-Length PSAT/NMSQT, PSAT 10, or PSAT 8/9 Practice
body:
If you take a full-length practice test for any of the PSAT-related assessments, your scores will be available on My Practice. Make sure you sign in to My Practice the same way you signed in to Bluebook to see your practice test scores.

If you take a practice test more than once, you'll just see one listing for it on the Past tab under Practice and Prepare. But when you go to My Practice, each completed test will be listed.
