The AP World History: Modern Exam has 2 sections and lasts 3 hours and 15 minutes. Section I has 2 parts.

Section I, Part A: Multiple Choice

The multiple-choice part has 55 questions and lasts 55 minutes. This part represents 40% of your total score. Your score on the multiple-choice part is based on the number of questions answered correctly. Points are not deducted for incorrect answers or unanswered questions.

Section I, Part B: Short Answer

The short-answer part has 3 short-answer questions and lasts 40 minutes. This part represents 20% of your total score for the exam, and each of the 3 questions counts equally toward your score.

Section II: Free Response

The free-response section has 1 document-based question (DBQ) and 1 long essay question and lasts 1 hour and 40 minutes. This section represents 40% of your total score for the exam. The DBQ represents 25% of your score on the exam, and the long essay question represents 15% of your score on the exam.

Taking the Exam

Each section and part is timed separately. You can go back and forth between questions in a section or part until time expires. The clock will turn red when 5 minutes remain in the section or part—the proctor will not give you any time updates or warnings. You cannot move ahead to a different section or part. Once time expires in a section or part, you cannot return to it.

You may use scratch paper for notes and planning, but credit will only be given for responses entered in this application. Any text you enter as an annotation will not be included in your answer submissions. When time expires in a section or part, all answers you have already entered will be submitted.

Source materials may have been edited for the purpose of this exam.

The inclusion of source material in this exam is not intended as an endorsement by College Board of the content, ideas, or values expressed in the material. The sources that appear in the AP World History: Modern Exam represent a range of different authors, historical periods, and perspectives, as appropriate for measuring the college-level knowledge and skills that are the focus of this course. AP students are not expected or asked to subscribe to any specific cultural or political values, but they are expected to analyze perspectives that may be different from their own and to analyze and interpret sources in historical context.

There may be references in AP testing materials to companies, products, and brands that are owned by others and subject to trademark law. Neither College Board nor the AP testing materials are affiliated with or endorsed by these trademark owners.

The AP English Literature and Composition Exam has 2 sections and lasts 3 hours.

Section I: Multiple Choice

The multiple-choice section has 55 questions and lasts 1 hour. This section represents 45% of your total score. Your score on the multiple-choice section is based on the number of questions answered correctly. Points are not deducted for incorrect answers or unanswered questions.

Section II: Free Response

The free-response section has 3 questions and lasts 2 hours. This section represents 55% of your total score. Each of the 3 questions counts equally toward your score.

Taking the Exam

Each section is timed separately. You can go back and forth between questions in a section until time expires. The clock will turn red when 5 minutes remain in the section—the proctor will not give you any time updates or warnings. You cannot move ahead to a different section. Once time expires in a section, you cannot return to it.

You may use scratch paper for notes and planning, but credit will only be given for responses entered in this application. Any text you enter as an annotation will not be included in your answer submissions. When time expires in a section, all answers you have already entered will be submitted.

The inclusion of source material in this exam is not intended as an endorsement by College Board of the content, ideas, or values expressed in the material. The literary works and excerpts that appear in the AP English Literature and Composition Exam represent a range of different authors and literary styles and themes, as appropriate for measuring the critical reading and analytic writing skills that are the focus of this college-level course. AP students are not expected or asked to subscribe to any specific cultural or political values, but they are expected to analyze perspectives that may be different from their own and to question the meaning, purpose, or effect of such content within literary works.

There may be references in AP testing materials to companies, products, and brands that are owned by others and subject to trademark law. Neither College Board nor the AP testing materials are affiliated with or endorsed by these trademark owners.

title: SAT Pilot Terms & Conditions
body:
Introduction 

These Terms and Conditions (“Terms and Conditions” or “Agreement”) are a legal contract between you and College Board (“College Board” or “we”). They set forth important rules and policies you must follow related to taking the Pilot SAT (“Pilot”). Please read these carefully. If you register for the Pilot on behalf of another (for example, if you are a parent or legal guardian of the test taker), these Terms and Conditions govern both you and the test taker (collectively, “you”). 

Background. The purpose of the Pilot is to provide information to College Board relating to its internal test development process. The Pilot will be provided digitally, and it will allow College Board, including its SAT® (“SAT”) program, to test certain questions and the digital format of the assessment.  You will not receive scores or feedback on your responses nor can the Pilot be used by you for college admission, placement, scholarships, or other purposes.  You understand that this exam is a pilot and College Board is under no obligation to include the format or new questions in a generally available offering. 

Additional COVID-19 related requirements may be communicated to you prior to or on test day. You agree to abide by such requirements. 
 
All disputes between you and College Board will be resolved through binding arbitration in accordance with Section 8 of this Agreement. You understand that by agreeing to arbitration, you are waiving your right to resolve disputes in a court of law by a judge or jury. 

Section 1. Preparing to Take the Pilot 

  • The Pilot is taken at a testing center. The Pilot is administered on a digital testing platform (“Pilot App”) that you download to your testing device.   
  • You will need a Personal PC laptop or Mac Laptop (your “Testing Device”) that connects to Wi-Fi. You cannot take the Pilot on a Chromebook, tablet, mobile phone, or on a school managed device.  Your testing device must run Windows 8 or later (PC users) or Mac OS 10.11 or later (Mac users). You may need to update your operating system. 
  • You will need to download the Pilot App to your Testing Device and complete Exam Setup not later than the day before the Pilot.  The Pilot App will be available for download starting five days before the Pilot.  When you complete exam setup, the Pilot App will generate an admissions ticket. 
  • On the day of the Pilot, you will need to physically check in to the test center at the designated time using your admissions ticket.  You may use your mobile phone to display your admissions ticket, however phones will be collected prior to testing and returned at the end of the test. You must bring a current government-issued or school-issued photo ID.  Additional ID may be required by the test center.  If you have been approved for testing accommodations, you will need your SSD Student Accommodations Letter. 
  • Once in your testing room, you will need to complete Pilot App check-in on your Testing Device, for which you will first need to connect to the test center’s Wi-Fi network. The exam will begin as soon as you successfully enter the exam start code into the application. 
  • Your Testing Device must be fully charged. If your testing device does not have at least three hours of battery life, you may wish to bring a portable charger. The test center is not responsible for device charging.   

Section 2.  Taking the Pilot  

  • Navigating the Pilot Questions. Each section of the Pilot has two parts, called modules. Once you move on from a module, you cannot return to any questions from it. 
  • Managing Your Time. The Pilot App will have a timer, counting down the minutes and seconds remaining in each module. You can hide the timer, but once there are 5 minutes remaining, you cannot hide the timer. When time expires, your work will be automatically saved and submitted. You will not be able to keep working on a question after time expires. 
  • Answer Submission. You will enter your answers in the Pilot App. You cannot work in any other program or application while the test is running, and you cannot paste work into the Pilot App from another program or application. You will not be submitting any handwritten work, and you will not be uploading any files or photos. Your answers are “submitted” when they are received by College Board.  If your testing device is connected to the internet when the exam ends, your answers will be automatically submitted to College Board.  If your device is NOT connected to the internet when the test ends, you will need to connect to the internet and follow directions in the Pilot App.  Answers must be received by College Board immediately after the Pilot, but in every event, must be received within 5 days of the end of the test.  

Section 3. Prohibited Items  

You may not bring prohibited items to the Pilot. Prohibited items include, but are not limited to: 

  • Mobile phones*, smartwatches*, fitness trackers, or other wearable technology (simple digital non-smartwatches or analog watches are acceptable).  

          *You can bring mobile phones and smartwatches (to show your admission ticket at check-   
            in) but you will be required to be store them or they will be or collected during the Pilot in accordance
            with the test center’s collection process. 

  • Audio players or recorders, tablets, laptops, notebooks, Bluetooth devices (e.g., wireless earbuds/ headphones), or any other personal computing devices other than your Testing Device 
  • Separate timers of any type 
  • Cameras or any other photographic equipment 
  • Books or references of any kind except as approved as an English language learner support for in-school administrations 
  • Compasses, rulers, protractors, or cutting devices 
  • Papers of any kind (scratch paper will be provided by a test proctor) 
  • Calculators (the Pilot App has a built-in calculator) 
  • Earplugs 
  • Weapons or firearms.      

NOTE: Some exceptions to the above may apply if a test taker has received a College Board–approved accommodation. 

Section 4. Prohibited Behaviors 

You may not engage in the prohibited behaviors set forth below: 

  • Attempting to cheat or otherwise obtain an unfair advantage on the Pilot. 
  • Obtaining, or attempting to obtain, improper access to the Pilot, or a part of the Pilot, or information about the Pilot. 
  • Accessing or attempting to access a phone, electronic device or any other Prohibited Items during testing or during breaks. 
  • Leaving the testing room, building, or designated break area without permission and/or taking an unapproved extended break. 
  • Reproducing or attempting to reproduce any portion of any Pilot in any form (e.g., by taking photos or making photocopies). 
  • Sharing Pilot content during or after the exam through any means, including, but not limited to, email, text messages, phone calls, photographs, social media, or the internet. 
  • Having subject-related information on your clothing, shoes, or body. 
  • Using testing accommodations not approved by College Board. 
  • Attempting to remove from the testing room any scratch paper or notes related to the Pilot. 
  • Copying the work of another student. 
  • Submitting any work that is not entirely your own.  
  • Attempting to give or get assistance, or otherwise communicate, through any means, with another person about the Pilot, during the Pilot administration, or after the Pilot administration.  
  • Attempting to take or taking the exam for someone else. 
  • Attempting to have or having someone else take the exam on your behalf. 
  • Creating a disturbance. 
  • Engaging in confrontational, threatening or unruly behavior, conduct or communication toward or concerning any test taker, test administrator or proctor, or employee of College Board or its vendors 
  • Failing to follow any of the test administration rules set forth in these Terms and Conditions, the Instructions, or in other registration materials, or directions given by the testing staff. 
  • Consume food or drink in unauthorized areas/times. 

Section 5. Privacy 

(a) Privacy Policies

College Board recognizes the importance of protecting your privacy. Our privacy policies located at collegeboard.org/privacy-center (“Privacy Policies”) are part of these Terms and Conditions. You consent to College Board’s collection, use, and disclosure of your personally identifiable information as described in the Privacy Policies and in these Terms and Conditions. College Board may update its Privacy Policies from time to time and they are subject to change up to one week prior to your test date. You are required to review the Privacy Policies located at collegeboard.org/privacy-center prior to taking the Pilot. 

(b) Testing 

i. Device Data: When you download and use the Pilot App, College Board will receive certain information about your device, including device type, operating system type and version, applications and processes running on your device, screen size and resolution, running processes, available memory, and other information to ensure the device is compatible. 

ii. Activity Data: We also monitor the actions you take in the Pilot App, including your responses, where you click, how long you spend on each page, and how you navigate through the Pilot  App. 

iii. Device Data and Activity Data (collectively, “Pilot Test Data”) may be used for College Board’s test security purposes as well as to develop and improve College Board products and services. Pilot Test Data may be disclosed to trusted vendors, but only in their provision of services to College Board. Pilot Test Data is not sold or licensed to third parties including without limitation for their marketing purposes. You will also be asked to type specific sentences in the Pilot App. Those typed sentences are not used for biometric identification.   

Section 6. Miscellaneous 

a. In the event of a test security related concern, public health threat, natural disaster, terrorist act, civil unrest, epidemic, or other unexpected events or circumstances, College Board may cancel testing for all or a specific group of test takers. In addition, College Board may cancel at any time due to issues related to COVID-19 in College Board’s sole discretion. If this occurs, College Board will notify you in advance, if feasible. 

b. To ensure the integrity of the Pilot, for security reasons, or for other reasons in our sole discretion, College Board reserves the right to bar any individual or group of individuals from registering for and/or taking any College Board assessment. 

c. College Board reserves the right to contact any appropriate individuals or agencies—including your high school—if we believe you may be in imminent danger of harming yourself or others, based on any information you provide to College Board, including in your responses to Pilot questions. We might also provide other content, along with your personal information, to those we contact. 

d. Each College Board contractor is a third-party beneficiary and is entitled to the rights and benefits under this Agreement and may enforce the provisions of this Agreement as if it were a party to this Agreement. 

e. College Board is not responsible for providing an internet connection or for internet service interruptions or errors outside of College Board’s control, such as data transmission errors on the public internet. 

f. College Board is not responsible for any equipment failures. 

g. College Board is not responsible for personal property, including prohibited items, brought to the Pilot that are lost, stolen, or damaged. 

h. College Board is not responsible for your failure to follow directions and instructions relating to the taking the Pilot. 

i. After successfully completing the Pilot, we will send you a link to a survey via email and upon your completion of the survey, you will receive a US $100 gift card (or other gift as communicated to you) as a thank you for your participation in the Pilot.   

Section 7. Intellectual Property Rights 

a. The Pilot, all College Board tests, pilot tests, test-related documents and materials, and test preparation materials (“Test Content”) are copyrighted works owned by College Board and protected by the laws of the United States and other countries. 

b. All software, webpages, algorithms, processes, and technologies, including the Pilot App, through which you access and take the Pilot, your answers are scored, and the test is secured and proctored, but excluding your device, your internet service provider (ISP) and the public internet, (collectively, the “Test Platform”) belong to College Board and its licensors. 

c. You shall not screenshot or attempt to make any image, copy, or download Pilot Test Content or the Pilot Test Platform. You shall not attempt to decompile, reverse engineer, or dissemble the Pilot Test Platform. 

d. All answers and answer documents you submit including all essay responses, portfolios, and audio or visual work are owned by the College Board, and these may be used by College Board for any purpose, subject to the Privacy Policies located at collegeboard.org/privacy-center, and in these Terms and Conditions. 

Section 8. ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES AND CLASS ACTION WAIVER 

a. All disputes between you and College Board and/or any or all of its contractors that relate in any way to registering for, participating in, or taking Pilot , but excluding all claims that a party violated the intellectual property rights of the other party, shall exclusively be resolved by a single arbitrator through binding, individual arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”) under the AAA Consumer Arbitration Rules in effect at the time a request for arbitration is filed with the AAA. Copies of the AAA Rules can be located at adr.org. Any dispute as to arbitrability shall be resolved by the arbitrator.  

b. Arbitration will be conducted on a documents-only basis (i.e., there will be no in-person or telephone hearing) unless otherwise agreed by the parties or required by the arbitrator. Should the parties agree to or the arbitrator requires proceedings, such proceedings should be conducted at a location which is reasonably convenient to both parties with due consideration of their ability to travel and other pertinent circumstances. If the parties are unable to agree on a location, the parties agree that the proceedings will be conducted via a video or telephonic call or, in the event that face-to-face proceedings are agreed to by the parties or required by the arbitrator, at a location that is reasonably convenient to both parties in accordance with the AAA Consumer Arbitration Rules.  

c. title: In-App Calculator
body: Calculator: On all math questions, you'll find a built-in calculator at the top right of the screen (you can also use your own approved calculator). On some exams, you'll see more than one kind of calculator—use whichever one you prefer.

title: Digital Testing Accommodations: SAT Suite
body:
Some testing accommodations work differently on the digital SAT than on the paper version of the test. Other accommodations may not be needed for a digital SAT. On your personal info page, Bluebook will list only the accommodations that apply to your digital SAT. 

If you’re approved for one of these accommodations, here’s how it’ll work in Bluebook.

AccommodationHow it Works in Bluebook
Extended Time

You’ll receive your approved amount of extended time and extra breaks. Once the standard time has elapsed on a module, section or part, you can move on when you are ready. 

Extended time for reading will be applied to the entire test. Extended time for math will only be applied to the Math section. Note: For SAT Weekend, if you’re approved for up to time and one-half and double time, you’ll test in a test center on a Saturday or Sunday.

Breaks as NeededYou’ll be able to pause the test time to take breaks as needed. The pause button appears below the timer. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra BreaksYou’ll get an extra 5-minute break between modules 1 and 2 in each section. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra and Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’, and you’ll have extra breaks. There is no pause button; you simply take the extra breaks for the length of time applied in Bluebook.
Braille (Refreshable Braille for Digital)You can use a screen reader, text-to-speech or refreshable braille. If you use a screen reader or text-to-speech, you’ll need to use headphones, too.  
Raised Line DrawingsYou’ll take the test in Bluebook, and you’ll receive a raised line supplement.
Braille WriterYou’ll use braille writing software to take the test.
Large-Print Exam, Large Print Answer Sheet, Magnification Device (Electronic/Non-Electronic)You can zoom using your device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).
Color Overlay/Color ContrastYou can use the color settings available through your operating system and/or device screen, or you can use a plastic overlay attached to your device's screen.
Human Reader for Digital Tests

Most students who use a human reader for paper exams are approved for Text-to-Speech (Embedded) and/or Screen Reader (Non-Embedded) for digital tests and will test digitally. You will use the built-in text-to-speech tool in Bluebook or the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board–approved screen reader software. In rare conditions, a student who is unable to test with text-to-speech or a screen reader may be approved in SSD Online for the accommodation of human reader for digital tests. 

Screen Reader (Non-Embedded)You can use the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board approved screen reader software (JAWS, NVDA, etc.). In addition to reading all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers), your screen reader will also read all properties of the page (headers, footers, punctuation) and provide detailed descriptions of graphs and figures. And you’ll get time and one-half (+50%) on your test.  
Text-to-Speech (Embedded) You can use the text-to-speech tool in Bluebook to read all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers) and short descriptions of graphics. 
Human Scribe for Digital Assessments You can use a human scribe to record the responses in Bluebook. You will test in a one-to-one setting. 
Dictation for Digital ExamsYou can use speech-to-text functionality on your test. Note: This is not a tool within the Bluebook application; it is the same functionality that you use with other applications.
Assistive Technology (AT)You can use your approved assistive technology software.
4-Function CalculatorYou can use a calculator on all math questions on the test. Use the Desmos calculator that’s built into the app, or bring your own approved calculator.
Limited TimeIf the test time exceeds your approved time, you will test over multiple days.
Auditory Amplification/FM SystemYou can test with your FM system, and you can use headphones. The proctor should use a handheld mic to give you the instructions.

help_items.title: Find Your Approved Accommodations
help_items.body: If you have a College Board–approved accommodation, you should’ve received a letter from our SSD office (“SSD” stands for Services for Students with Disabilities). For more information, visit accommodations.collegeboard.org.

help_items.title: How to Apply for an Accommodation
help_items.body: For most accommodations, the easiest thing to do is to have your school’s SSD coordinator apply for the accommodation on your behalf. (“SSD” stands for Services for Students with Disabilities.) If you’re not sure who the SSD coordinator is at your school, ask your counselor. For more information, visit accommodations.collegeboard.org.

help_items.title: Selecting Accommodations for Practice Tests
help_items.body: You’re encouraged to apply accommodations to your full-length practice test so you can get a feel for how accommodations work with digital exams. But selecting accommodations on a practice test does not mean those accommodations will be applied to your actual test. On test day, only College Board–approved accommodations will be applied to your digital exam.

help_items.title: Assistive Technology
help_items.body:
Any approved assistive technology that you use when you’re online should still work during your exam. If you use assistive technologies (AT), such as screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, ChromeVox, ZoomText Fusion, etc.) to interact with a standard web browser, the same commands can be used to navigate through content in the digital exam. The exception to this would be if you use a web-based assistive technology or a browser extension.

If you use assistive technology, open/start the AT device or software before you open Bluebook for practice and on exam day. On exam day, adjust any necessary settings before you start to check in for the digital exam. Exceptions are noted when configuration is not required ahead of the exam.

help_items.title: Zoom and Magnification
help_items.body:
Chromebook Zoom and Magnification

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use the magnification feature, select the options from the floating accessibility menu:

  • Full-screen magnifier (Search + Ctrl + M) — whole-screen magnification
    • Adjust the full-screen magnifier from the floating Accessibility menu > Settings > Display and magnification > Full screen magnifier > select any of these options:
      • Move screen continuously as mouse moves
      • Move screen keeping mouse at center of screen
      • Move screen when mouse touches edge of screen (default)
  • Docked magnifier (Search + Ctrl + D) — split-screen magnification
    • To adjust zoom level, select the down arrow in the Docked zoom level.
    • To change what’s magnified, move your pointer or press Tab.

 

Windows Zoom and Magnifier

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use Windows Magnifier:  

  • Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Vision: Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Or press the Windows logo key + plus sign (+). To turn off the Magnifier, press the Windows logo key + Esc.

Adjust the Magnifier view per your preference:  

  • Lens (Ctrl + Alt + L)
  • Full screen (Ctrl + Alt + F)
  • Docked (Ctrl + Alt + D)

 

MacOS Zoom

To zoom in/out, press Command +/-. To reset zoom, press Command + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To customize how the zoom area appears, go to Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility and click Zoom on the right (keyboard shortcut: Option + Command + 8).

In the Advanced Options, select the checkboxes for your zoom preference:  

  • Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom
  • Use trackpad gesture to zoom
  • Use scroll gesture with modifier keys to zoom

Select Zoom style options per student preference:  

  • Full screen
  • Split screen
  • Picture-in-picture

 

iPad Zoom

Pinch to zoom in or zoom out.

For additional zoom options in the iPad, tap Settings > Accessibility > Zoom.

Adjust any of the following:

  • Keyboard shortcuts: Control zoom using shortcuts on an external keyboard.
  • Zoom controller: Turn the controller on, set controller actions, and adjust the color and opacity.
  • Zoom region: Choose Pinned Zoom, Full Screen Zoom, or Window Zoom.
  • Zoom filters: Choose None, Inverted, Grayscale, Grayscale Inverted, or Low Light.
  • Maximum zoom level: Drag the slider to adjust the level.

help_items.title: Verbal Instructions
help_items.body:
Your proctor will read this aloud: 
 
Welcome. Today you’re taking the SAT, an important step toward your college and career goals.  

Please listen carefully to these instructions. When I finish, I’ll give you the start code. If you haven’t completed check-in yet, pause while I read. You can finish checking in later. 

If you’d like to follow along as I read these instructions, click Review the Instructions. If you’re not on the start code screen yet, click Help and then Verbal Instructions. 

You agreed to follow the rules and keep test content confidential. I will dismiss anyone who tries to break the rules, and their scores will be canceled. They may also be prevented from taking College Board tests in the future. 

Bluebook should be the only application open on your device unless you’re using approved assistive technology. Other open applications will be detected and could result in score cancellation. 

Close all other applications now. Does anyone need to close other applications? 

Your proctor will pause so you can close any other applications, then they’ll read this: 

Bluebook times everyone individually and will tell you when it’s time to take your break. You might start your break at slightly different times than your neighbor, so please be quiet at all times. 

To take a break at any other time, go to the More menu and click Unscheduled Break. You will lose testing time if you take an unscheduled break. 

If you have an approved accommodation for breaks as needed, select Pause under the timer instead so you don’t lose testing time. 

I’ll come around soon to make sure you cleared your desk as instructed in Bluebook. I’ll also give you any materials related to your accommodations. And if you brought a calculator, I’ll make sure it’s acceptable. 

If you have phones, smartwatches, or other prohibited devices, turn them off now. 

You should have 1 sheet of scratch paper, which I’ll collect after the test so don’t tear it. Write your full name in the top right corner. If you don’t have one, let me know when I come by your desk. 

If students in your room are approved for certain accommodations, you'll hear additional instructions: 

For students testing with a screen reader: If you’re using text-to-speech, a screen reader, or other approved assistive technology, now is the time to make sure it’s working. Remember, you can use the built-in features on your device. More information is available on the Bluebook Help page. 

For students testing with a human reader: Readers must read questions aloud as often as requested. It’s important that they read only exactly what is in the script. They must not elaborate, even if the student asks. 

For students testing with a scribe: Scribes must write only the answers and corrections that students dictate. They can’t prompt the student in a way that would result in a different response. Scribes will read student answers back to them if students want to review their work. 

For students testing with raised line drawings: The raised line drawings have the same labels and numbers as the detailed descriptions you’ll hear. 

Then your proctor will read this: 

Please pay attention to these final instructions.  

Don’t leave until I confirm your answers are submitted and dismiss you. Don’t close your laptop or cover your tablet before then. I’ve posted a reminder here. You’ll receive official scores you can use to apply to college. If you want to cancel your scores, let me know in the next 5 days. 

If you need help or extra scratch paper at any time, raise your hand and I’ll come over. Remember to write your full name on extra scratch paper. 

Does anyone have any questions?  

Your proctor will answer any final questions, then they’ll read this: 
I’ll give you the start code in a moment. When you enter the code and click Start Test, your timer will start and you can begin testing. 

If you don’t see the start code screen yet, finish checking in.  

I’ll read the start code now and write it on the board. Good luck!

help_items.title: Screen Magnification
help_items.body: Screen magnification technology enlarges the content displayed on the computer screen in order to assist students with visual impairments. Although the exam app supports some non-embedded screen magnifier tools from third parties, all users can zoom using their device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).

help_items.title: Text-to-Speech
help_items.body:
If you’re approved for the accommodation “Text-to-Speech (Embedded),” then a built-in text-to-speech (TTS) tool will be available whenever you test with Bluebook. You don’t need to do anything to configure this tool.  

Use the Play/Pause button to hear entire passages or engage Click Mode to hear specific sentences. 

You can adjust voice selection, speed, or volume of the playback.

If you're testing on a Mac or iPad and you're approved for embedded text-to-speech, you can now choose from any voices previously downloaded to the device in addition to standard Bluebook options.

help_items.title: Speech-to-Text
help_items.body:
Chromebook Dictation

Chromebook provides two options for using the dictation feature for items requiring text entry:  

  • Dictation: From the floating accessibility menu, select Dictation.
  • Speak with the onscreen keyboard: From the floating accessibility menu select Onscreen keyboard. At the top of the onscreen keyboard, select Speak (microphone).
    • You can move, float, dock, and resize the onscreen keyboard. 


Tap or select where you want to type (input field, free-response questions, essays, etc.). Press Search + D or  Launcher + D.

 

Windows Speech

To use Windows Speech, follow the steps below for your operating system:

Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Speech > Turn on Speech Recognition.

Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Speech > Turn on Voice Access.

  • Keyboard shortcut: Press Windows logo key + Ctrl + S to turn on speech recognition.


Tip: For Windows 10 or 11, to help with navigation and selecting elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “19, OK”).

 

MacOS Voice Control

To use Voice Control on a Mac, go to System Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control.

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Voice Control Guide > Open Guide.

 

iPad Voice Control

To start using Voice Control on an iPad, go to Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control. 

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Open Voice Control Guide.

help_items.title: MathJax
help_items.body:
Bluebook implements MathJax technology to: 

  • Display mathematical content, such as expressions, equations, and inequalities elegantly in browsers. 
  • Provide students who use screen readers with MathCAT access to off-screen accessible MathML for both UEB and Nemeth braille support with refreshable braille displays. 
  • Access a variety of accessibility features via menus attached to the MathJax content to assist students with low vision and students that need highlighted rendering. 
     

MathJax objects within Bluebook exams are custom-configured to function with all mainstream text-to-speech and screen-reading assistive technologies across all supported operating systems. This custom configuration ensures that all mainstream assistive technologies will read the textual alternatives without additional configurations. 
 

Optional MathJax configurations (UEB Support)  
Some students may prefer to navigate complex math equations and math expressions with math viewers or plugins like MathCAT with personal screen readers like JAWS and NVDA.   
To explore MathML content, you can press Alt + M (Windows and Chromebook) or Option + M (Mac and iOS) to turn graphic mode on/off. When graphic mode is turned off, students can access the MathML and choose UEB or Nemeth from MathCAT. 

Alternatively, hidden MathML can be enabled via the MathJax context menu via Options > Include Hidden MathML
 
NOTE: This action can be set once at the start of an exam, and it will persist throughout the duration. The student may press Alt + M (or Option + M) again to revert to the default “graphic mode on” configuration or by activating Reset to defaults within the MathJax Settings (context menu).

help_items.title: Screen Readers
help_items.body:
Chromebook ChromeVox

To enable ChromeVox, press Ctrl + Alt + Z or select it from the floating accessibility menu.

Note: If you're approved to use a screen reader and you don't see the floating accessibility menu on your Chromebook, let someone at your school know right away.

If ChromeVox turns off when you launch the Bluebook app or at any time, you can turn it back on with Ctrl + Alt + Z.

Test content can be navigated with the keyboard. Depending on your keyboard, you can press the Search or Launcher key for some shortcuts. Both keys work the same way.

 

Basic keyboard navigation: Use the keyboard shortcuts if parts of the content are not initially reading.
ActionKeyboard Shortcut
Read items on a pageSearch or Launcher + right arrow (or left arrow to move back)
Go to the next/previous lineSearch or Launcher + up/down arrow
Start reading from the current locationSearch or Launcher + R
Stop/pause readingCtrl

 

Windows Narrator

To start or stop Narrator, press the Windows logo key + Ctrl + Enter together. 

Important: The Narrator key is a modifier key in the Narrator commands. Both the Caps Lock and Insert keys are the Narrator key by default. The Narrator key is referred to as “Narrator” in commands.

 

Basic keyboard navigation:

help_items.title: Refreshable Braille Displays
help_items.body:
RBDs are used to read text-only content on digital exams. Alternative text descriptions are embedded in the exams for all graphics. RBDs must be properly set up before they can be used by students. Refreshable braille is not recommended for students that require tactile graphics. Students can request a braille exam or raised line drawings.

help_items.title: Digital Testing Accommodations: SAT Suite
help_items.body:
Some testing accommodations work differently on the digital SAT than on the paper version of the test. Other accommodations may not be needed for a digital SAT. On your personal info page, Bluebook will list only the accommodations that apply to your digital SAT. 

If you’re approved for one of these accommodations, here’s how it’ll work in Bluebook.

AccommodationHow it Works in Bluebook
Extended Time

You’ll receive your approved amount of extended time and extra breaks. Once the standard time has elapsed on a module, section or part, you can move on when you are ready. 

Extended time for reading will be applied to the entire test. Extended time for math will only be applied to the Math section. Note: For SAT Weekend, if you’re approved for up to time and one-half and double time, you’ll test in a test center on a Saturday or Sunday.

Breaks as NeededYou’ll be able to pause the test time to take breaks as needed. The pause button appears below the timer. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra BreaksYou’ll get an extra 5-minute break between modules 1 and 2 in each section. There is no pause button; you will simply take the length of break that is applied in Bluebook.
Extra and Extended BreaksYour section break will be twice as long as other test takers’, and you’ll have extra breaks. There is no pause button; you simply take the extra breaks for the length of time applied in Bluebook.
Braille (Refreshable Braille for Digital)You can use a screen reader, text-to-speech or refreshable braille. If you use a screen reader or text-to-speech, you’ll need to use headphones, too.  
Raised Line DrawingsYou’ll take the test in Bluebook, and you’ll receive a raised line supplement.
Braille WriterYou’ll use braille writing software to take the test.
Large-Print Exam, Large Print Answer Sheet, Magnification Device (Electronic/Non-Electronic)You can zoom using your device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).
Color Overlay/Color ContrastYou can use the color settings available through your operating system and/or device screen, or you can use a plastic overlay attached to your device's screen.
Human Reader for Digital Tests

Most students who use a human reader for paper exams are approved for Text-to-Speech (Embedded) and/or Screen Reader (Non-Embedded) for digital tests and will test digitally. You will use the built-in text-to-speech tool in Bluebook or the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board–approved screen reader software. In rare conditions, a student who is unable to test with text-to-speech or a screen reader may be approved in SSD Online for the accommodation of human reader for digital tests. 

Screen Reader (Non-Embedded)You can use the screen reader available through your device's operating system or any College Board approved screen reader software (JAWS, NVDA, etc.). In addition to reading all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers), your screen reader will also read all properties of the page (headers, footers, punctuation) and provide detailed descriptions of graphs and figures. And you’ll get time and one-half (+50%) on your test.  
Text-to-Speech (Embedded) You can use the text-to-speech tool in Bluebook to read all text (reading passages, math problems and equations, and multiple-choice response questions/answers) and short descriptions of graphics. 
Human Scribe for Digital Assessments You can use a human scribe to record the responses in Bluebook. You will test in a one-to-one setting. 
Dictation for Digital ExamsYou can use speech-to-text functionality on your test. Note: This is not a tool within the Bluebook application; it is the same functionality that you use with other applications.
Assistive Technology (AT)You can use your approved assistive technology software.
4-Function CalculatorYou can use a calculator on all math questions on the test. Use the Desmos calculator that’s built into the app, or bring your own approved calculator.
Limited TimeIf the test time exceeds your approved time, you will test over multiple days.
Auditory Amplification/FM SystemYou can test with your FM system, and you can use headphones. The proctor should use a handheld mic to give you the instructions.

help_items.title: Find Your Approved Accommodations
help_items.body: If you have a College Board–approved accommodation, you should’ve received a letter from our SSD office (“SSD” stands for Services for Students with Disabilities). For more information, visit accommodations.collegeboard.org.

help_items.title: How to Apply for an Accommodation
help_items.body: For most accommodations, the easiest thing to do is to have your school’s SSD coordinator apply for the accommodation on your behalf. (“SSD” stands for Services for Students with Disabilities.) If you’re not sure who the SSD coordinator is at your school, ask your counselor. For more information, visit accommodations.collegeboard.org.

help_items.title: Selecting Accommodations for Practice Tests
help_items.body: You’re encouraged to apply accommodations to your full-length practice test so you can get a feel for how accommodations work with digital exams. But selecting accommodations on a practice test does not mean those accommodations will be applied to your actual test. On test day, only College Board–approved accommodations will be applied to your digital exam.

help_items.title: Assistive Technology
help_items.body:
Any approved assistive technology that you use when you’re online should still work during your exam. If you use assistive technologies (AT), such as screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, ChromeVox, ZoomText Fusion, etc.) to interact with a standard web browser, the same commands can be used to navigate through content in the digital exam. The exception to this would be if you use a web-based assistive technology or a browser extension.

If you use assistive technology, open/start the AT device or software before you open Bluebook for practice and on exam day. On exam day, adjust any necessary settings before you start to check in for the digital exam. Exceptions are noted when configuration is not required ahead of the exam.

help_items.title: Zoom and Magnification
help_items.body:
Chromebook Zoom and Magnification

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use the magnification feature, select the options from the floating accessibility menu:

  • Full-screen magnifier (Search + Ctrl + M) — whole-screen magnification
    • Adjust the full-screen magnifier from the floating Accessibility menu > Settings > Display and magnification > Full screen magnifier > select any of these options:
      • Move screen continuously as mouse moves
      • Move screen keeping mouse at center of screen
      • Move screen when mouse touches edge of screen (default)
  • Docked magnifier (Search + Ctrl + D) — split-screen magnification
    • To adjust zoom level, select the down arrow in the Docked zoom level.
    • To change what’s magnified, move your pointer or press Tab.

 

Windows Zoom and Magnifier

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use Windows Magnifier:  

  • Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Vision: Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Or press the Windows logo key + plus sign (+). To turn off the Magnifier, press the Windows logo key + Esc.

Adjust the Magnifier view per your preference:  

  • Lens (Ctrl + Alt + L)
  • Full screen (Ctrl + Alt + F)
  • Docked (Ctrl + Alt + D)

 

MacOS Zoom

To zoom in/out, press Command +/-. To reset zoom, press Command + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To customize how the zoom area appears, go to Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility and click Zoom on the right (keyboard shortcut: Option + Command + 8).

In the Advanced Options, select the checkboxes for your zoom preference:  

  • Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom
  • Use trackpad gesture to zoom
  • Use scroll gesture with modifier keys to zoom

Select Zoom style options per student preference:  

  • Full screen
  • Split screen
  • Picture-in-picture

 

iPad Zoom

Pinch to zoom in or zoom out.

For additional zoom options in the iPad, tap Settings > Accessibility > Zoom.

Adjust any of the following:

  • Keyboard shortcuts: Control zoom using shortcuts on an external keyboard.
  • Zoom controller: Turn the controller on, set controller actions, and adjust the color and opacity.
  • Zoom region: Choose Pinned Zoom, Full Screen Zoom, or Window Zoom.
  • Zoom filters: Choose None, Inverted, Grayscale, Grayscale Inverted, or Low Light.
  • Maximum zoom level: Drag the slider to adjust the level.

help_items.title: Verbal Instructions
help_items.body:
Your proctor will read this aloud:  

Welcome. Today you’re taking the SAT, an important step toward your college and career goals. 

Please listen carefully to these instructions. When I finish, I’ll give you the start code. If you haven’t completed check-in yet, pause while I read. You can finish checking in later. 

If you’d like to follow along as I read these instructions, click Help and then Verbal Instructions.  

You agreed to follow the rules and keep test content confidential.  

I will dismiss anyone who tries to break the rules, and their scores will be canceled. They may also be prevented from taking College Board tests in the future.  

Bluebook should be the only application open on your device unless you’re using approved assistive technology. Other applications will be detected and could result in score cancellation. 

Close all other applications now.  

Does anyone need more time to close other applications?  

The proctor will pause while you close all other applications, then they’ll read this: 

Bluebook times everyone individually, and it will tell you when it’s time to take your break. You might start your break at slightly different times than your neighbor, so please be quiet at all times. 

To take a break at any other time, go to the More menu and click Unscheduled Break. You will lose testing time if you take an unscheduled break.  

If you have an approved accommodation for breaks as needed, select Pause instead so you don’t lose testing time.  

You’ll receive official scores that you can use to apply to college. If you want to cancel your scores, you go to collegeboard.org/mysat within 1 week from today. 

I’ll come around soon to collect prohibited items and make sure you cleared your desk as instructed in Bluebook. If you brought a calculator, I’ll make sure it’s acceptable. 

Keep your photo ID on your desk. If you leave the room, bring it with you. If you have phones, smartwatches, or other prohibited devices, turn them off before I collect them. You should have 1 sheet of scratch paper, which I’ll collect after the test. Write your full name at the top right corner. If you don’t have one, let me know when I come by your desk.   

After your proctor checks student desks, they’ll read this: 
  
Please pay attention to these final instructions. 

When the test ends, raise your hand and I’ll confirm your answers are submitted and dismiss you. Don’t leave, close your laptop, or cover your tablet before then. I’ve posted a reminder here. 

If you need help or extra scratch paper at any time, raise your hand and I’ll come over. Remember to write your full name on extra scratch paper. 

Does anyone have any questions?  

After your proctor pauses to answer questions, they’ll read this:   
 
I’ll give you a start code in a moment. When you enter the code and click Start Test, your timer will start and you can begin testing.  

If you don’t see the start code screen yet, finish checking in.   

I’ll read the start code now and write it on the board. Good luck!

help_items.title: Screen Magnification
help_items.body: Screen magnification technology enlarges the content displayed on the computer screen in order to assist students with visual impairments. Although the exam app supports some non-embedded screen magnifier tools from third parties, all users can zoom using their device’s native controls (Control +/- on a PC; Command +/- on a Mac; pinch and zoom on an iPad).

help_items.title: Text-to-Speech
help_items.body:
If you’re approved for the accommodation “Text-to-Speech (Embedded),” then a built-in text-to-speech (TTS) tool will be available whenever you test with Bluebook. You don’t need to do anything to configure this tool.  

Use the Play/Pause button to hear entire passages or engage Click Mode to hear specific sentences. 

You can adjust voice selection, speed, or volume of the playback.

If you're testing on a Mac or iPad and you're approved for embedded text-to-speech, you can now choose from any voices previously downloaded to the device in addition to standard Bluebook options.

help_items.title: Speech-to-Text
help_items.body:
Chromebook Dictation

Chromebook provides two options for using the dictation feature for items requiring text entry:  

  • Dictation: From the floating accessibility menu, select Dictation.
  • Speak with the onscreen keyboard: From the floating accessibility menu select Onscreen keyboard. At the top of the onscreen keyboard, select Speak (microphone).
    • You can move, float, dock, and resize the onscreen keyboard. 


Tap or select where you want to type (input field, free-response questions, essays, etc.). Press Search + D or  Launcher + D.

 

Windows Speech

To use Windows Speech, follow the steps below for your operating system:

Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Speech > Turn on Speech Recognition.

Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Speech > Turn on Voice Access.

  • Keyboard shortcut: Press Windows logo key + Ctrl + S to turn on speech recognition.


Tip: For Windows 10 or 11, to help with navigation and selecting elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “19, OK”).

 

MacOS Voice Control

To use Voice Control on a Mac, go to System Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control.

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Voice Control Guide > Open Guide.

 

iPad Voice Control

To start using Voice Control on an iPad, go to Settings > Accessibility > enable (turn on) Voice Control. 

Tip: To help navigate and select elements in Bluebook, say “show numbers.” Numbers will appear on the screen for every element/grid in the active window. Say an item’s corresponding number to select it (e.g., “Click 19, OK”).

Recommended: Learn and practice Voice Control commands in the interactive guide. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control > Open Voice Control Guide.

help_items.title: MathJax
help_items.body:
Bluebook implements MathJax technology to: 

  • Display mathematical content, such as expressions, equations, and inequalities elegantly in browsers. 
  • Provide students who use screen readers with MathCAT access to off-screen accessible MathML for both UEB and Nemeth braille support with refreshable braille displays. 
  • Access a variety of accessibility features via menus attached to the MathJax content to assist students with low vision and students that need highlighted rendering. 
     

MathJax objects within Bluebook exams are custom-configured to function with all mainstream text-to-speech and screen-reading assistive technologies across all supported operating systems. This custom configuration ensures that all mainstream assistive technologies will read the textual alternatives without additional configurations. 
 

Optional MathJax configurations (UEB Support)  
Some students may prefer to navigate complex math equations and math expressions with math viewers or plugins like MathCAT with personal screen readers like JAWS and NVDA.   
To explore MathML content, you can press Alt + M (Windows and Chromebook) or Option + M (Mac and iOS) to turn graphic mode on/off. When graphic mode is turned off, students can access the MathML and choose UEB or Nemeth from MathCAT. 

Alternatively, hidden MathML can be enabled via the MathJax context menu via Options > Include Hidden MathML
 
NOTE: This action can be set once at the start of an exam, and it will persist throughout the duration. The student may press Alt + M (or Option + M) again to revert to the default “graphic mode on” configuration or by activating Reset to defaults within the MathJax Settings (context menu).

content.content: Please click Next to complete check-in, then the app will lock down your device. Do not attempt to run any other applications while the exam is in progress.

title: We're About to Lock Your Device

content.content: If you attempt to use other programs or apps during the exam, your scores will be canceled.
Notes, books, or any other reference materials.
Headphones or earbuds—unless you have a College Board–approved accommodation.
Smart glasses, a smartphone, smartwatch, or any other connected device.
Any camera, recording device, or timer.
You may use the scratch paper provided by your proctor. You may not bring you own scratch paper.

Some AP Exams require or allow a calculator. On these exams, a Desmos graphing calculator will be available on the Bluebook testing screens. You can also use your own approved calculator. 
 

Calculator Policies by Course
AP CourseCalculator Type
BiologyFour-function (with square root), scientific, or graphing calculator allowed.

Note: The Desmos graphing calculator is not available for this exam because Desmos does not currently have the required statistics computational capabilities.

Students won't benefit from using a calculator on digital versions of other AP Exams.

For further details on calculator policies, visit apstudents.org/calculators.

help_items.body: Calculator: On all math questions, you'll find a built-in calculator at the top right of the screen (you can also use your own approved calculator). On some exams, you'll see more than one kind of calculator—use whichever one you prefer.

help_items.title: Testing Timers
help_items.body:
During testing, a timer will let you know how much time remains for each module or part of the test.

At the end of section 1, you’ll have a short break. During the break, we’ll show you a timer counting down to the beginning of section 2.

When time runs out on section 2, the test will end, and your answers will be automatically submitted.

help_items.title: Highlights & Notes
help_items.body:
Highlights & Notes: Use this tool to highlight text and leave yourself notes. 

  • Click on Highlights & Notes from the top right of the screen.
    •  
  • Select some text to highlight.
    •  
  • You can change the highlight color, add an underline, make a note, or delete the highlight.
    •   
  • When you’re done, simply click outside the highlight.
    •  
  • You can click on a highlight any time to edit it.
    •  
This tool is available on Section 1 of the SAT Suite of Assessments and on all sections of AP Exams.

You cannot annotate pictures, buttons, or text that you enter.

If the content you annotate is shared across multiple questions, you’ll see your notes on all of those questions. Your notes will not be graded.

help_items.title: Option Eliminator
help_items.body: Option Eliminator: On any multiple-choice question, you can cross out answer options you think are wrong. Click the strikethrough button next to any answer option to cross it out (you can always undo this action). To turn off option eliminator mode, click the ABC button above the answer choices

help_items.title: Mark for Review
help_items.body: Mark for Review: Flag any question you want to come back to later.

help_items.title: Line Reader
help_items.body: Line Reader: This tool helps you focus as you’re reading test content. Click the six dots at the top of the line reader to move it up and down using your keyboard arrows. If you’re on a touch screen device, you can also move it with your finger. To see more than one line of text at a time, use the arrow button at the bottom of the line reader to change the number of visible lines.

help_items.title: Question Menu
help_items.body: At the bottom of each testing screen, you’ll find a menu that allows you to navigate to any question in the section. You’ll see which questions you’ve answered, which you haven’t, and any that you’ve marked for review.

help_items.title: Make an Educated Guess
help_items.body: If you’re trying hard on every question, it’s better to guess than to leave a question blank—especially if you can eliminate one or two answer options first.

help_items.title: Restarting the App
help_items.body: If Bluebook crashes during your exam, relaunch it, hit Resume Testing, and raise your hand so your proctor can check you back in to the exam. The testing timer will be paused until you resume testing.

help_items.title: Submitting Your Answers
help_items.body: During testing, the app will save all your work. When the exam is over, your answers will be submitted automatically. If you’re still working when time expires, your responses will be automatically saved and submitted. If your device is offline or your submission fails for any reason, you’ll have time to reconnect and submit your work.

help_items.title: Ending the Test Early
help_items.body: If you're approved for extra time, you can move on from a section or end the test before your full time expires, though we encourage you to use extra time to check your work. help_items.title: Exiting the App on a Chromebook

help_items.title: Zoom and Magnification
help_items.body:
Chromebook Zoom and Magnification

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use the magnification feature, select the options from the floating accessibility menu:

  • Full-screen magnifier (Search + Ctrl + M) — whole-screen magnification
    • Adjust the full-screen magnifier from the floating Accessibility menu > Settings > Display and magnification > Full screen magnifier > select any of these options:
      • Move screen continuously as mouse moves
      • Move screen keeping mouse at center of screen
      • Move screen when mouse touches edge of screen (default)
  • Docked magnifier (Search + Ctrl + D) — split-screen magnification
    • To adjust zoom level, select the down arrow in the Docked zoom level.
    • To change what’s magnified, move your pointer or press Tab.

 

Windows Zoom and Magnifier

To zoom in/out, press Control +/-. To reset zoom, press Control + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To use Windows Magnifier:  

  • Windows 10: Select Start > Settings > Ease of Access > Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Windows 11: Select Start > Settings > Accessibility > Vision: Magnifier > Turn on Magnifier.
  • Or press the Windows logo key + plus sign (+). To turn off the Magnifier, press the Windows logo key + Esc.

Adjust the Magnifier view per your preference:  

  • Lens (Ctrl + Alt + L)
  • Full screen (Ctrl + Alt + F)
  • Docked (Ctrl + Alt + D)

 

MacOS Zoom

To zoom in/out, press Command +/-. To reset zoom, press Command + 0.

For touchscreen and touchpad, pinch in/out.

To customize how the zoom area appears, go to Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility and click Zoom on the right (keyboard shortcut: Option + Command + 8).

In the Advanced Options, select the checkboxes for your zoom preference:  

  • Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom
  • Use trackpad gesture to zoom
  • Use scroll gesture with modifier keys to zoom

Select Zoom style options per student preference:  

  • Full screen
  • Split screen
  • Picture-in-picture

 

iPad Zoom

Pinch to zoom in or zoom out.

For additional zoom options in the iPad, tap Settings > Accessibility > Zoom.

Adjust any of the following:

  • Keyboard shortcuts: Control zoom using shortcuts on an external keyboard.
  • Zoom controller: Turn the controller on, set controller actions, and adjust the color and opacity.
  • Zoom region: Choose Pinned Zoom, Full Screen Zoom, or Window Zoom.
  • Zoom filters: Choose None, Inverted, Grayscale, Grayscale Inverted, or Low Light.
  • Maximum zoom level: Drag the slider to adjust the level.

help_items.title: In-App Calculator
help_items.body: Calculator: On all math questions, you'll find a built-in calculator at the top right of the screen (you can also use your own approved calculator). On some exams, you'll see more than one kind of calculator—use whichever one you prefer.

help_items.title: Approved Calculators
help_items.body:
Acceptable Calculators

Calculators permitted during testing include:

  • The Desmos calculator embedded in the Bluebook testing app: This is a powerful calculator that includes features similar to a handheld graphing calculator. If you are familiar with how to use this calculator, the embedded version is a good choice.
  • Graphing calculators that do not include CAS features: This type of calculator includes plotting and graphing windows, data entry and storage windows, data analysis functions, trig functions, and programming options.
  • Scientific calculators: This type of calculator includes many functions helpful for solving problems in science, statistics, and math. Common features include built-in memory to store interim calculations, statistical functions, pi, trig functions, and scientific notation.
  • Four-function basic calculators (not recommended): This type of calculator includes four functions: add, subtract, multiply, and divide; some also include percentages and square roots. This type of calculator is not recommended as they typically do not follow order of operations.
     

Prohibited Calculators

Calculators with the following features are prohibited:

  • Calculators with built-in CAS functionality. Examples of such devices include:
    • Casio: ClassPad 300, 330, or 400; ClassPad II (fx-CP400); ClassPad fx-CG 500 or fx-CG500; Algebra fx 2.0; all model numbers that begin with CFX-9970G.
    • Hewlett Packard: HP Prime; HP 48GII; all model numbers that begin with 40G, 49G, or 50G.
    • Texas Instruments: TI-Nspire CAS, TI-Nspire CX II CAS; All model numbers that begin with TI-89 or TI-92 or have "CAS" in the model name. Note that TI-Nspire models that do not include "CAS" in the name are acceptable.
  • Calculators with apps, menus, or programs that perform symbolic algebra manipulation (e.g., solving algebra equations symbolically).
  • Calculators with QWERTY keyboards.
  • Devices with wireless internet capability, Bluetooth, or cellular connectivity.
  • Devices with built-in cameras or audio/video recording.
  • Tablets and laptop computers.
  • Electronic writing pads or pen-input devices.
  • Cell phone calculator apps.
  • Calculators that use paper tape.

help_items.title: Highlights & Notes
help_items.body:
Highlights & Notes: Use this tool to highlight text and leave yourself notes. 

  • Click on Highlights & Notes from the top right of the screen.
    •  
  • Select some text to highlight.
    •  
  • You can change the highlight color, add an underline, make a note, or delete the highlight.
    •

    •  
  • You can click on a highlight any time to edit it.
    •  
This tool is available on Section 1 of the SAT Suite of Assessments and on all sections of AP Exams.

You cannot annotate pictures, buttons, or text that you enter.

If the content you annotate is shared across multiple questions, you’ll see your notes on all of those questions. Your notes will not be graded.

help_items.title: Line Reader
help_items.body: Line Reader: This tool helps you focus as you’re reading test content. Click the six dots at the top of the line reader to move it up and down using your keyboard arrows. If you’re on a touch screen device, you can also move it with your finger. To see more than one line of text at a time, use the arrow button at the bottom of the line reader to change the number of visible lines.

help_items.title: Option Eliminator
help_items.body: Option Eliminator: On any multiple-choice question, you can cross out answer options you think are wrong. Click the strikethrough button next to any answer option to cross it out (you can always undo this action). To turn off option eliminator mode, click the ABC button above the answer choices

help_items.title: Mark for Review
help_items.body: Mark for Review: Flag any question you want to come back to later.

help_items.title: Question Menu
help_items.body: At the bottom of each testing screen, you’ll find a menu that allows you to navigate to any question in the section. You’ll see which questions you’ve answered, which you haven’t, and any that you’ve marked for review.

help_items.title: Testing Timers
help_items.body:
During testing, a timer will let you know how much time remains for each module or part of the test.

At the end of section 1, you’ll have a short break. During the break, we’ll show you a timer counting down to the beginning of section 2.

When time runs out on section 2, the test will end, and your answers will be automatically submitted.
